41. Engineer in the White Spaces

作者：Michael Nygard

A system consists of interdependent programs. We call the arrangement of these programs and their relationships architecture . When we diagram these systems, we often represent individual programs or servers as simplistic little rectangles, connected by arrows.

系统由相互依赖的程序组成。我们把这些程序及其关系的排列叫架构。画系统图时，我们常把单个程序或服务器画成简单小方框，用箭头连起来。

One little arrow might mean, “Synchronous request/reply using SOAP-XML over HTTP. ” That’s quite a lot of information for one glyph to carry. There’s not usually enough room to write all that, so we label the arrow with either “XML over HTTP” from an internal perspective, or “SKU Lookup” for the external perspective.

一个小箭头可能意味着「用 SOAP-XML over HTTP 的同步请求/回复」。一个符号要承载这么多信息。通常没空间写全，所以箭头要么标内部视角的「XML over HTTP」，要么标外部视角的「SKU 查询」。

That arrow bridging programs looks like a direct contact, but it isn’t. The white space between the boxes is filled with hardware and software components. This substrate may contain:

那个跨程序的箭头看起来像直接联系，但不是。方框之间的空白里塞满了硬件和软件组件。这个基底可能包括：

Network interface cards •

网卡

Network switches •

网络交换机

Firewalls •

防火墙

IDS and IPS •

入侵检测/防御系统

Message queues or brokers •

消息队列或代理

XML transformation engines •

XML 转换引擎

FTP servers •

FTP 服务器

“Landing zone” tables •

「着陆区」表

Metro-area SoNET rings •

城域 SoNET 环网

MPLS gateways •

MPLS 网关

Trunk lines •

中继线

Oceans •

大洋

Cable-finding fishing trawlers •

找电缆的渔船

There will always be four or five computers between program A and B, running their software for packet switching, traffic analysis, routing, threat analysis, and so on. As the architect bridging those programs, you must consider this substrate.

程序 A 和 B 之间总会有四五台计算机，跑着包交换、流量分析、路由、威胁分析等软件。作为桥接这些程序的架构师，你必须考虑这个基底。

I saw one arrow labeled “Fulfillment”. One server was inside my client’s company, the other server was in a different one. That arrow, critical to customer satisfaction, unpacked a chain of events that resembled a game of “Mousetrap” more than a single interface. Messages went to message brokers that dumped to files, which were picked up by a periodic FTP job, and so on. That one “interface” had more than 20 steps.

我见过一个标着「履约」的箭头。一台服务器在客户公司内，另一台在另一家公司。那个对客户满意至关重要的箭头，拆开后是一串事件，更像「捕鼠器」游戏而不是单个接口。消息到消息代理，转储到文件，再被定期 FTP 任务取走，等等。那个「接口」有 20 多步。

It’s essential to understand the static and dynamic loads that arrow must carry. Instead of just “SOAP-XML over HTTP, ” that one little arrow should also say, “Expect one query per HTTP request and send back one response per HTTP reply. Expect up to 100 requests per second, and deliver responses in less than 250 milliseconds 99.999% of the time.”

理解那个箭头必须承载的静态和动态负载至关重要。不光是「SOAP-XML over HTTP」，那个小箭头还应该说：「每个 HTTP 请求期望一次查询、每个 HTTP 回复返回一次响应。期望每秒最多 100 个请求，99.999% 的时间在 250 毫秒内返回响应。」

There’s more we need to know about that arrow:

关于那个箭头我们还需要知道：

What if the caller hits it too often? Should the receiver drop requests on • the floor, refuse politely, or make the best effort possible?

调用方打太频繁怎么办？接收方该把请求丢地上、礼貌拒绝、还是尽力而为？

What should the caller do when replies take more than 250 milliseconds? • Should it retry the call? Should it wait until later, or assume the receiver has failed and move on without that function?

回复超过 250 毫秒时调用方该怎么办？该重试吗？该等以后再说，还是假设接收方挂了、不带这个功能继续走？

What happens when the caller sends a request with version 1.0 of the pro- • tocol and gets back a reply in version 1.1? What if it gets back some HTML instead of XML? Or an MP3 file instead of XML?

调用方发 1.0 版协议请求、收到 1.1 版回复会怎样？收到 HTML 而不是 XML 会怎样？收到 MP3 文件而不是 XML 呢？

What happens when one end of the interface disappears for a while? •

接口一端消失一阵会怎样？

Answering these questions is the essence of engineering the white spaces.

回答这些问题就是空白处工程的本质。

42. Talk the Talk

作者：Mark Richards

IN any profession, jargon is used so that individuals within that profession can effectively communicate with one another. Lawyers talk to one another about habeas corpus, voir dire, and venire; carpenters talk to one another about butt joints, lap joints, and flux; and software architects talk to one another about ROA, Two Step View, and Layer Supertype. Wait, what was that?

任何职业都有行话，让圈内人有效沟通。律师聊人身保护令、预先审核、陪审团人选；木匠聊对接榫、搭接榫、焊料；软件架构师聊 ROA、两步视图、层超类型。等等，那是什么？

It is imperative that software architects, regardless of the platform they are working in, have an effective means of communication among one another. One of those means of communication is through architecture and design patterns. To be an effective software architect you must understand the basic architecture and design patterns, recognize when those patterns are being used, know when to apply the patterns, and be able to communicate to other architects and developers using them.

软件架构师不管在什么平台上工作，都必须有彼此有效沟通的手段。其中一种手段就是架构和设计模式。要成为高效的软件架构师，你必须理解基本架构和设计模式、识别什么时候在用这些模式、知道什么时候该用、并能用它们和其他架构师及开发沟通。

Architecture and design patterns can be classified into four basic categories: enterprise architecture patterns, application architecture patterns, integration patterns, and design patterns. These categories are generally based on the level of scope within the overall architecture. Enterprise architecture patterns deal with the high-level architecture, whereas design patterns deal with how individual components within the architecture are structured and behave.

架构和设计模式可分四大类：企业架构模式、应用架构模式、集成模式和设计模式。这些类别通常按整体架构中的范围层次划分。企业架构模式处理高层架构，设计模式处理架构中单个组件如何结构化和行为。

Enterprise architecture patterns define the framework for the high-level architecture. Some of the more common architecture patterns include event-driven architecture (EDA), service-oriented architecture (SOA), resource-oriented architecture (ROA), and pipeline architecture.

企业架构模式定义高层架构的框架。一些常见架构模式包括事件驱动架构（EDA）、面向服务架构（SOA）、面向资源架构（ROA）和管道架构。

Application architecture patterns specify how applications or subsystems within the scope of a larger enterprise architecture should be designed. Some common pattern catalogs in this category include the well-known J2EE design

应用架构模式规定更大企业架构范围内的应用或子系统该怎么设计。这个类别里一些常见模式目录包括著名的 J2EE 设计

patterns (e.g., Session Façade and Transfer Object) and the application architecture patterns described in Martin Fowler’s book Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (Addison-Wesley Professional).

模式（比如 Session Façade 和 Transfer Object）以及 Martin Fowler《企业应用架构模式》（Addison-Wesley Professional）里描述的应用架构模式。

Integration patterns are important for designing and communicating concepts surrounding the sharing of information and functionality between components, applications, and subsystems. Some examples of integration patterns include file sharing, remote procedure calls, and numerous messaging patterns. You can find these patterns at http://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/eaipatterns.html .

集成模式对设计和沟通组件、应用、子系统间信息与功能共享的概念很重要。一些集成模式例子包括文件共享、远程过程调用和众多消息模式。

Knowing the basic design patterns as described by the Gang of Four book Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software (AddisonWesley Professional) is a must for any software architect. Although these patterns may appear to be too low-level for a software architect, they are part of a standard vocabulary that makes for effective communication between architects and developers.

知道四人帮《设计模式：可复用面向对象软件的基础》（Addison-Wesley Professional）描述的基本设计模式是每个软件架构师的必备。虽然这些模式对软件架构师可能显得太低层，但它们是标准词汇的一部分，让架构师和开发之间有效沟通。

It is also important to be aware of and understand the various anti-patterns as well. Anti-patterns , a term coined by Andrew Koenig, are repeatable processes that produce ineffective results. Some of the more well-known anti-patterns include Analysis Paralysis, Design By Committee, Mushroom Management, and Death March. Knowing these patterns will help you avoid the many pitfalls you will most likely experience. You can find a list of the common antipatterns at http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-patterns .

了解和理解各种反模式也很重要。反模式这个词是 Andrew Koenig 提出的，指产生无效结果的可重复过程。一些更知名的反模式包括分析瘫痪、委员会设计、蘑菇管理、死亡行军。知道这些模式帮你避开很可能遇到的陷阱。

Software architects need the ability to communicate with one another in a clear, concise, and effective way. The patterns are there; it is up to us as software architects to learn and understand these patterns so we can “walk the walk and talk the talk.”

软件架构师需要清晰、简洁、有效沟通的能力。模式就在那里；我们软件架构师要做的就是学习和理解这些模式，好让我们「走得正、说得对」。

43. Context Is King

作者：Edward Garson

I feel there is a certain irony  in trying to impart something about architectural ideals, when the very premise I wish to begin with is that effectively there are no ideals. If this is indeed the case, then surely there is nothing to write; I am a contradiction and by doing this I run the risk of the universe imploding or something like that.

我觉得有点讽刺：我想传授一些关于架构理想的东西，而我想开篇的前提却是实际上没有理想。如果真是这样，那当然没东西可写；我是个矛盾体，这么做我冒着宇宙内爆之类的风险。

But alas, ceci n’est pas une pipe .

可是，这不是一只烟斗。

One of the most valuable lessons that I have learned as a software architect is that context is king, and simplicity its humble servant. What this means in practical terms is that context is the only force that trumps simplicity when you’re making architectural decisions.

作为软件架构师学到的最有价值的一课是：上下文为王，简单是它谦卑的仆人。实际意思是：做架构决策时，上下文是唯一能压倒简单的力量。

When I say context , I refer not only to high-level, immediate forces such as key business drivers, but also to elements in the periphery, such as emerging technologies and thought leadership on diverse topics. Indeed, good architects keep track of several fast-moving targets.

我说的上下文，不仅指高层、即时的力量比如关键业务驱动因素，还指边缘元素，比如新兴技术和各种话题上的思想领导力。好架构师同时追踪好几个快速移动的目标。

What constitutes good architecture? It is the product of decisions made within a context usually tainted with multiple competing priorities. Those competing priorities mean that sometimes the most important decisions are not about what you put in, but rather what you omit. The currency of good architecture is simply astute decision-making (while the products are all only about communicating your intent).

什么是好架构？它是在一个通常被多个竞争优先级污染的上下文中做出的决策的产物。那些竞争优先级意味着有时候最重要的决策不是关于你放什么，而是关于你省略什么。好架构的通货就是精明的决策（而产品都只是关于沟通你的意图）。

Historically, there have been some fascinating examples of the influence that context can have on architecture. A favorite example involves the database selected to support an ambitious new software system for a modern battlefield

历史上有一些上下文如何影响架构的迷人例子。我最喜欢的一个涉及为一个现代战场雄心勃勃的新软件系统选数据库

tank. 1 (Deciding what database to use is not usually architecturally significant; this example merely serves to illustrate a point.)

坦克。（决定用什么数据库通常不是架构上重要的事；这个例子只是为了说明一个观点。）

When it came time to choose the database, the team assessed many. It found that while the tank was moving quickly over undulating terrain while tracking a target, the majority of the databases were capable of supporting the maximal throughput required of the navigation and targeting systems. But the team was taken by surprise when it discovered that firing the main gun on the tank caused such a strong electromagnetic pulse that it totally crashed the onboard systems and of course the database along with it! On a modern battlefield, a tank without its software running is quite literally in the dark. In this context, recovery time was the overwhelming factor in the choice of database, and no database did that better at the time than InterBase, 2 and that is why it was chosen for the M1 Abrams tank.

选数据库时，团队评估了很多。它发现虽然坦克在起伏地形上快速移动跟踪目标，大多数数据库都能支持导航和瞄准系统所需的最大吞吐。但团队意外发现：坦克主炮开火产生的电磁脉冲太强，会让车载系统彻底崩溃、当然数据库也一起崩！在现代战场上，一辆没有软件跑着的坦克字面意义上是瞎的。在这个上下文里，恢复时间是选数据库的压倒性因素，当时没有数据库比 InterBase 做得更好，这就是它被选用于 M1 艾布拉姆斯坦克的原因。

So, while newsgroups rage with the flames of technology debates of X versus Y, it is idle amusement. The reason these debates rage is often not because of huge disparities in their technical merits, but rather because there are more subtle differences between them, and what features individuals value more than others when there is no guiding context to act as a trump card.

所以，当新闻组里 X 对 Y 的技术辩论吵得火热时，那是无聊的消遣。这些辩论吵起来通常不是因为技术优劣差异巨大，而是因为差异更微妙，以及在没有引导性上下文当王牌时，个人更看重哪些特性。

Your team should be free of ideals, reflect on context in the first instance, and reach for the simplest solutions from there.

你的团队应该没有理想，首先反思上下文，然后从那里找最简单的方案。

1 A tank, despite its extremely dubious purpose, is still an engineering marvel. 2 Interestingly, InterBase had an architecture that caused disk-writes to leave the database in an always-consistent state. This is one reason that contributes to its ability to recover from hard failures so quickly.

1 坦克尽管用途极可疑，仍是工程奇迹。2 有趣的是，InterBase 的架构让磁盘写入使数据库始终处于一致状态。这是它能从硬故障快速恢复的原因之一。

44. Dwarves, Elves, Wizards, and Kings

作者：Evan Cofsky

In Neal Stephenson’s novel Cryptonomicon (EOS), Randy Waterhouse explains his classification system for the different types of people he meets. Dwarves are hard workers, steadily producing beautiful artifacts in the dark loneliness of their caves. They exert tremendous forces moving mountains and shaping earth, and are renowned for their craftsmanship. Elves are elegant, cultured, and spend their days creating new and beautiful magical things. They are so gifted they don’t even realize that other races view these things as otherworldly almost. The wizards are immensely powerful beings almost completely unlike all others, but unlike the elves, they do know about magic and its power and nature, and they wield it with supreme effect. But there is a fourth type of character that Waterhouse alludes to but does not mention specifically. The kings are the visionaries who know what must be done with all of these different characters.

在 Neal Stephenson 的小说《Cryptonomicon》（EOS）里，Randy Waterhouse 解释他对遇到的不同类型人的分类系统。矮人是勤劳的人，在洞穴黑暗孤独中稳定地生产精美制品。他们移动山脉、塑造大地，以工艺著称。精灵优雅、有教养，整天创造新奇美丽的魔法东西。他们太有天赋，甚至没意识到其他种族把这些东西看作超凡脱俗。巫师是无比强大的存在，几乎和所有其他种族都不同，但和精灵不同，他们确实知道魔法及其力量和本质，并以极致效果运用它。但 Waterhouse 还暗示了第四种角色但没具体提。国王是知道该用所有这些不同角色做什么的有远见者。

An architect is a king of sorts. The architect must be familiar with all of these characters, and ensure that the architecture has roles for all of them. An architecture designed only for one will attract only that one character to the project, and even with the best dwarves, or elves, or wizards, the team will be severely limited in its reach if it can only approach problems in one way.

架构师是一种国王。架构师必须熟悉所有这些角色，确保架构为他们都提供位置。只为一种角色设计的架构只会吸引那种角色到项目里，即使有最好的矮人、精灵或巫师，如果团队只能用一种方式解决问题，它的覆盖面也会严重受限。

A good king will lead all types through a quest, and help them work together to complete it. Without the quest, there is no vision for the team, and it ultimately becomes a partisan mess. Without all the characters, the team can only solve one class of problem, and is stopped at the first barrier impassable to that solution.

好国王会带领所有类型完成一个任务，帮他们一起合作完成。没有任务，团队就没有愿景，最终变成派系混战。没有所有角色，团队只能解决一类问题，遇到那个方案过不去的第一道障碍就停了。

The architect creates the quest with all the characters in mind. The architecture then becomes a guide for finding tasks for the different characters to perform while learning about one another. When a project encounters difficulty, the team will already know how to approach solving it because the architecture gave them the opportunities to grow into a team.

架构师在创建任务时把所有角色放在心上。架构于是成为为不同角色找任务、同时互相了解的指南。项目遇到困难时，团队已经知道怎么解决，因为架构给了他们成长为团队的机会。

Evan Cofsky Evan Cofsky is a software engineer, an amateur musician, and an avid cyclist. He studied both music and computer science in college, and continues to study them. Currently he is a senior software engineer with Virgin Charter as its resident Python expert, and works with an eclectic team of exceptionally bright and diverse people.

Evan Cofsky Evan Cofsky 是软件工程师、业余音乐家和狂热骑行者。他在大学学了音乐和计算机科学，现在还在学。他目前是 Virgin Charter 的高级软件工程师和驻场 Python 专家，和一群特别聪明、多元的人一起工作。

45. Learn from Architects of Buildings

作者：Keith Braithwaite

Architecture is a social act and the material theater of human activity.

建筑是一种社会行为，是人类活动的物质剧场。

—Spiro Kostof

——Spiro Kostof

How many software architects  see their role as exclusively, or primarily, technical? Is it not rather that they are the conciliators, go-betweens and arbiters of the warring factions among the stake-holders? How many approach their work in a purely intellectual spirit, without giving proper weight to the human factors of their job?

有多少软件架构师把自己的角色看作纯粹、或主要是技术性的？他们难道不更是干系人之间交战派系的调解人、中间人和仲裁者？有多少人以纯粹理智的精神做工作，而没有给工作中人的因素适当权重？

A great architect is not made by way of a brain nearly so much as he is made by way of a cultivated, enriched heart.

伟大的建筑师与其说是大脑造就的，不如说是被修养丰富的心造就的。

—Frank Lloyd Wright

——Frank Lloyd Wright

What more strongly marks out the architects in your organization: raw intellectual horsepower and vast capacity to recall technical minutiae, or taste, refinement, and generosity of spirit? Under which tendency would you prefer to work?

在你的组织里，什么更能标志出架构师：原始智力马力和回忆技术细节的巨大能力，还是品味、修养和精神慷慨？你更愿意在哪个倾向下工作？

A doctor can bury his mistakes but an architect can only advise his client to plant vines.

医生可以埋葬他的错误，但建筑师只能建议客户种葡萄藤。

—ibid

——同上

Is the “maintenance” of “legacy” systems anything more than pruning those vines? Would you, as an architect, have the intestinal fortitude to scrap a piece of work that had failed? Or would you cover it up? Wright also said that the architect’s best friend was the sledgehammer. What have you demolished recently?

「遗产」系统的「维护」难道不就是修剪那些葡萄藤吗？作为架构师，你有胆量报废一件失败的作品吗？还是会掩盖它？Wright 还说建筑师最好的朋友是大锤。你最近拆了什么？

Architects believe that not only do they sit at the right hand of God, but that if God ever gets up, they take the chair.

建筑师相信他们不仅坐在上帝右手边，而且上帝一旦起身，他们就坐那把椅子。

—Karen Moyer

——Karen Moyer

For “God,” read “customer.”

把「上帝」读成「客户」。

In architecture as in all other operative arts, the end must direct the operation. The end is to build well. Well building has three conditions: Commodity, Firmness and Delight.

在建筑和所有其他操作性艺术中，目的必须指导操作。目的是建造得好。好的建造有三个条件：坚固、实用、愉悦。

—Henry Watton

——Henry Watton

When was the last time you saw a piece of software whose architecture gave you any delight? Do you aim to give delight with your work?

你上次看到一件软件的架构给你愉悦是什么时候？你旨在用你的工作给人愉悦吗？

No person who is not a great sculptor or painter can be an architect. If he is not a sculptor or painter, he can only be a builder

不是伟大雕塑家或画家的人不能成为建筑师。如果他不是雕塑家或画家，他只能是建造者。

—John Ruskin

——John Ruskin

Does artistry play its proper part in your architecture? Is the assemblage of components to make systems informed by a painterly concern for shape and texture, a sculptural sense of balance and implied motion, or the importance of negative space?

艺术感在你的架构里起了恰当作用吗？组件组成系统时，是否带着画家对形状和质感的关注、雕塑家对平衡和暗示运动的感觉、或者留白的重要性？

And finally, no gloss is required on this comment, a sure remedy for the software architect’s most damaging syndrome.

最后，这句话不需要任何修饰，它是软件架构师最具破坏性综合征的解药。

It seems a fantastic paradox, but it is nevertheless a most important truth, that no architecture can be truly noble which is not imperfect.

这看起来像个奇妙悖论，但仍是最重要的真理：不完美的建筑不可能真正高贵。

—ibid

——同上

46. Fight Repetition

作者：Niclas Nilsson

Are your developers performing recurring tasks that need little thinking? Can you find recurring patterns in the code? Can you spot code that’s been written copy-paste-modify style? If that’s the case, your team is moving slower than it should and, oddly enough, you may be the cause.

你的开发在做不需要怎么思考的重复任务吗？你能在代码里找到重复模式吗？你能发现复制-粘贴-修改风格写的代码吗？如果是这样，你的团队比应该的慢，而且奇怪的是，原因可能是你。

Before explaining why, let’s agree on a couple of truths about software ­development:

解释为什么之前，我们先就软件开发的几个真理达成一致：

Duplication is evil. •

重复是罪恶。

Repetitive work slows down development. •

重复工作拖慢开发。

As an architect, you set the tone. You’ve got the best overall grasp of the system and you probably wrote a trend-setting, end-to-end, vertical slice of the system that serves as an example for the team—an example that has been copied many times by now. Whenever a developer copies anything—be it a few lines of code, an XML file, or a class—that’s a clear indication that something could be made simpler or even completely abstracted away. Most often, it’s not the domain logic that is copied; it’s the infrastructure code that just has to be there to make it work. For that reason, it’s crucial that you can envision the effects your examples have. Any code and configuration in your examples will be the base for tens, hundreds, or maybe thousands of other slices of the system, which means you have to make sure that your code is clean, intention revealing, and containing nothing except what can’t be abstracted away: the domain problem itself. As an architect, you need to be highly sensitive to any kind of repetitive patterns, since anything you write will (ironically) be repeated.

作为架构师，你定基调。你对系统整体把握最好，你大概写了一个引领趋势的端到端垂直切片作为团队样板——一个现在已被复制很多次的样板。每当开发复制任何东西——几行代码、一个 XML 文件、或一个类——那都是某个东西可以被简化甚至完全抽象掉的明确信号。最常被复制的不是领域逻辑；而是那些必须在那里才能工作的基础设施代码。因此，你能预见你的样板产生什么影响至关重要。你样板里的任何代码和配置将成为系统几十、几百、也许几千个其他切片的基础，意味着你必须确保代码干净、意图明显、除了不能抽象掉的东西——领域问题本身——什么都没有。作为架构师，你需要对任何重复模式高度敏感，因为你写的任何东西（讽刺地）都会被重复。

But that doesn’t happen in your system, right? Take a look at that configuration file. What needs to be different if applied on another slice of the system, and what will stay the same? Look at a typical business layer method. Is there a pattern that shows up in other methods as well, containing things like transaction handling, logging, authentication, or auditing? How about the data access layer? Any code in there that will be the same except for names of entities and fields? Look broader. Can you find two or three lines of code that frequently seem to go together, and even though they operate on different objects, feel like the same thing? These are all examples of repetition. Repetition in code is something that developers eventually learn to filter out and ignore when reading the code, once they figure out where the interesting variabilities are found, but even if the developers get used to it, it slows them down. Code like that is clearly written for computers to execute, not for developers to read.

但那不会发生在你的系统里，对吧？看看那个配置文件。如果应用到系统另一个切片，什么需要不同、什么保持相同？看一个典型业务层方法。有没有一个模式也出现在其他方法里，包含事务处理、日志、认证或审计之类的东西？数据访问层呢？那里除了实体和字段名之外一样的代码？看宽一点。你能找到两三行经常一起出现的代码吗——即使它们操作不同对象，感觉像同一个东西？这些都是重复的例子。代码里的重复，开发最终学会在阅读时过滤掉、忽略掉——一旦他们搞清楚有趣的变体在哪——但即使开发习惯了，它也拖慢他们。那样的代码显然是写给计算机执行的，不是写给开发读的。

Your responsibility is to remove it. To do that, you may need to harvest frameworks, create better abstractions, perhaps ask the toolsmith to set up an aspect framework or write a few small code generators, but the repetition won’t go away unless someone does something about it.

你的责任是去掉它。为此，你可能需要收获框架、创建更好的抽象、也许请工具师搭一个切面框架或写几个小代码生成器，但重复不会消失，除非有人做点什么。

That someone is you.

那个人是你。

47. Welcome to the Real World

作者：Gregor Hohpe

Engineers like precision, especially software engineers who live in the realm of ones and zeros. They are used to working with binary decisions, one or zero, true or false, yes or no. Everything is clear and consistent, guaranteed by foreign key constraints, atomic transactions, and checksums.

工程师喜欢精确，尤其生活在 0 和 1 世界里的软件工程师。他们习惯二元决策：一或零、真或假、是或否。一切都清晰一致，由外键约束、原子事务和校验和保证。

Unfortunately, the real world is not quite that binary. Customers place orders, only to cancel them a moment later. Checks bounce, letters are lost, payments delayed, and promises broken. Data entry errors are bound to happen every so often. Users prefer “shallow” user interfaces, which give them access to many functions at once without being boxed into a lengthy, one-dimensional “process,” which is easier to program and seems more “logical” to many developers. Instead of the call stack controlling the program flow, the user is in charge.

不幸的是，现实世界没那么二元。客户下订单，转眼又取消。支票跳票、信件丢失、付款延迟、承诺打破。数据录入错误免不了时不时发生。用户偏好「浅」用户界面，一次访问很多功能而不是被框进漫长一维的「流程」——后者更容易编程、对很多开发也更「逻辑」。不是调用栈控制程序流，而是用户在掌舵。

Worse yet, widely distributed systems introduce a whole new set of inconsistencies into the game. Services may not be reachable, change without prior notice, or do not provide transactional guarantees. When you run applications on thousands of machine, failure is no longer a question of “if,” but of “when.” These systems are loosely coupled, asynchronous, concurrent, and do not adhere to traditional transaction semantics. You should have taken the blue pill!

更糟的是，广泛分布的系统给游戏引入了一整套新的不一致。服务可能不可达、无预告变更、或不提供事务保证。在几千台机器上跑应用时，失败不再是「如果」而是「何时」。这些系统松耦合、异步、并发，不遵循传统事务语义。你本该吃蓝色药丸的！

As computer scientists’ brave new world is crumbling, what are we to do? As is so often the case, awareness is a first important step toward a solution.

随着计算机科学家的美丽新世界崩塌，我们该怎么办？和往常一样，觉察是走向解决方案的第一步。

Say goodbye to the good old predictive call-stack architecture, where you get to define what happens when and in what order. Instead, be ready to respond to events at any time in any order, regaining your context as needed. Make asynchronous requests concurrently instead of calling methods one by one. Avoid complete chaos by modeling your application using event-driven process chains or state models. Reconcile errors through compensation, retry, or tentative operations.

告别美好的、可预测的调用栈架构——在那里你能定义什么时候发生什么、按什么顺序。相反，准备好随时按任何顺序响应事件，需要时恢复上下文。并发发异步请求，而不是一个一个调方法。用事件驱动过程链或状态模型建模应用以避免完全混乱。通过补偿、重试或试探操作协调错误。

Sounds scary and more than you bargained for? Luckily, the real world has to deal with the same issues for a long time: delayed letters, broken promises, messages crossing in transit, payments posted to the wrong account—the examples are countless. Accordingly, people had to resend letters, write off bad orders, or tell you to ignore the payment reminder in case you already sent a payment. So don’t just blame the real world for your headaches, but also use it as a place to look for solutions. After all, Starbucks does not two-phase commit, either. 1 Welcome to the real world.

听起来吓人、超出你预期？幸运的是，现实世界很久以来就在处理同样的问题：延迟的信件、打破的承诺、交叉的消息、记错账户的付款——例子数不清。相应地，人们不得不重发信件、勾销坏订单、或者告诉你如果已经付过款就忽略付款提醒。所以别只是把你的头痛怪到现实世界头上，也把它当找解决方案的地方。毕竟星巴克也不做两阶段提交。欢迎来到现实世界。

Gregor Hohpe Gregor Hohpe is a software architect with Google, Inc. Gregor is a widely recognized thought leader on asynchronous messaging architectures and serviceoriented architectures. He coauthored the seminal book Enterprise Integration Patterns (Addison-Wesley Professional) and speaks regularly at technical conferences around the world. 1 See http://www.eaipatterns.com/ramblings/18_starbucks.html .

Gregor Hohpe Gregor Hohpe 是 Google 的软件架构师。Gregor 是异步消息架构和面向服务架构领域广泛认可的思想领袖。他合著了开创性的《企业集成模式》（Addison-Wesley Professional），经常在全球技术会议演讲。

48. Don't Control, but Observe

作者：Gregor Hohpe

Today’s systems are distributed and loosely coupled. Building loosely coupled systems is a bit of a drag, so why do we bother? Because we want our systems to be flexible so they do not break apart at the slightest change. This is a critical property in today’s environments, where we may only control a small portion of our application, the remainder living in distributed services or third-party packages, controlled by other departments or external vendors.

今天的系统是分布式、松耦合的。建松耦合系统有点麻烦，那我们为什么还要费这个劲？因为我们想要系统灵活，这样它不会在 slightest 变化时散架。这在今天的环境里是关键属性——我们可能只控制应用的一小部分，其余活在分布式服务或第三方包中，被其他部门或外部厂商控制。

So, it looks like the effort to build a system that is flexible and can evolve over time is a good idea. But that also means our system will change over time. As in “today’s system is not what it was yesterday.” Unfortunately, this makes documenting the system challenging. It’s commonly known that documentation is out of date the moment it is printed, but in a system that changes all the time, things can only be worse. Moreover, building a system that is flexible generally means the architecture is more complex and it’s more difficult to get the proverbial “big picture.” For example, if all system components communicate with one another over logical, configurable channels, one better have a look at the channel configuration to get any idea what is going on. Sending messages into the logical la-la-land is unlikely to trigger a compiler error, but it is sure to disappoint the user whose action was encapsulated in that message.

所以，建一个灵活、能随时间演化的系统看起来是好主意。但那也意味着我们的系统会随时间变化。就像「今天的系统不是昨天的系统」。不幸的是，这让记录系统变得有挑战。众所周知文档一印出来就过时，但在一个一直在变的系统里，情况只会更糟。此外，建灵活系统通常意味着架构更复杂，更难得到那个众所周知的「大局」。比如，如果所有系统组件通过逻辑可配置通道通信，你最好看看通道配置才知道在发生什么。把消息发到逻辑的 la-la-land 不会触发编译错误，但肯定会让那个动作被封装在消息里的用户失望。

Being a control-freak architect is so yesteryear, leading to tightly coupled and brittle solutions. But letting the software run wild is sure to spawn chaos. You have to supplement the lack of control with other mechanisms to avoid doing an instrument flight without the instruments. But what kind of instruments do

做控制狂架构师是过气了，导致紧耦合和脆弱的方案。但让软件乱跑肯定会滋生混乱。你必须用其他机制补充控制的缺失，避免没有仪表就做仪表飞行。但我们有什么仪表？

we have? Plenty, actually. Today’s programming languages support reflection, and almost all runtime platforms provide runtime metrics. As your system becomes more configurable, the current system configuration is another great source of information. Because so much raw data is difficult to understand, extract a model from it. For example, once you figure out which components send messages to which logical channels, and which components listen to these channels, you can create a graph model of the actual communication between components. You can do this every few minutes or hours, providing an accurate and up-to-date image of the system as it evolves. Think of it as “Reverse MDA.” 1 Instead of a model driving the architecture, you build a flexible architecture, and extract the model from the actual system state.

其实很多。今天的编程语言支持反射，几乎所有运行时平台提供运行时指标。随着系统变得更可配置，当前系统配置是另一个大好信息源。因为太多原始数据难以理解，从中提取一个模型。比如，一旦搞清楚哪些组件发消息到哪些逻辑通道、哪些组件监听这些通道，你就能创建组件间实际通信的图模型。你可以每隔几分钟或几小时做一次，提供系统演化过程中准确、最新的图像。把它想成「反向 MDA」。不是模型驱动架构，而是你建一个灵活架构，从实际系统状态提取模型。

In many cases, it’s easy to visualize this model, creating the literal big picture. However, resist the temptation to plot the 3×5-meter billboard of boxes and lines, which contains every class in your system. That picture may pass as contemporary art, but it’s not a useful software model. Instead, use a 1,000-foot view as described by Erik Doernenburg, a level of abstraction that actually tells you something. On top of that, you can make sure your model passes basic validation rules, such as the absence of circular dependencies in a dependency graph, or no messages being sent to a logical channel no one listens to.

很多情况下，把这个模型可视化很容易，创造字面意义的大图。然而，抵制画那个 3×5 米的方框和线条广告牌的诱惑——它包含你系统里每个类。那幅画可能算当代艺术，但不是有用的软件模型。相反，用 Erik Doernenburg 描述的 1000 英尺视角——一个真正告诉你东西的抽象层次。在此之上，你可以确保模型通过基本验证规则，比如依赖图里没有循环依赖、或没有消息发到没人听的逻辑通道。

Letting go of control is a scary thing, even when it comes to system architecture. But supplemented by observation, model extraction, and validation, it is probably the way only to architect for the 21st century.

放手控制是吓人的事，即使在系统架构领域。但辅以观察、模型提取和验证，这大概是为 21 世纪做架构的唯一方式。

1 MDA = model-driven architecture.

1 MDA = 模型驱动架构。

49. Janus the Architect

作者：David Bartlett

In the Roman world, Janus was the god of beginnings and endings, doors and passageways. Janus is usually depicted with two heads facing in different directions, a symbol you may have seen on coins or in the movies. Janus represents transitions and changes in life from past to future, young to old, marriage, births, and coming of age.

在罗马世界，Janus 是开始与结束、门与通道之神。Janus 通常被描绘成两个头朝不同方向，这个符号你可能在硬币或电影上见过。Janus 代表生命中从过去到未来、年轻到年老、婚姻、出生、成年的过渡和变化。

For any architect, software or structural, Janus’s ability to see forward and backward or past to future is a highly regarded skill. An architect strives to merge realities with vision; past success with future direction; business and management expectations with development constraints. Creating these bridges is a major part of being an architect. Often an architect may feel she is trying to span chasms while bringing a project to completion because of different forces acting on a project—for example, ease of access versus security or satisfying present business processes while designing for management’s future vision. A good architect must have those two heads capable of carrying two different ideas or thoughts, different goals or visions, to create a product that will satisfy the various project stakeholders.

对任何架构师——软件或结构——Janus 向前向后、从过去到未来看的能力是备受推崇的技能。架构师力求把现实与愿景融合；过去成功与未来方向融合；业务和管理期望与开发约束融合。创建这些桥梁是架构师的主要部分。架构师经常觉得她在完成项目时试图跨越深渊，因为作用在项目上的力量不同——比如易访问性 vs 安全，或满足当前业务流程同时为管理未来愿景设计。好架构师必须有那两个头，能承载两个不同想法或思想、不同目标或愿景，来创建满足各项目干系人的产品。

You should notice that Janus has two heads, not simply two faces. This allows Janus to have the extra ears and eyes needed for awareness. An excellent IT architect will be a superior listener and evaluator. Understanding the reason for a capital expenditure is crucial to determining the goals and vision a management team has for the future of its organization. Being able to evaluate the technical skills of your staff with the design and technology to be used within the project will aid in creating the proper training and programming pairs to ensure a successful project. Knowing what open source solutions to use in combination with common off-the-shelf software can greatly streamline a project’s timelines and budgets. An excellent architect will be aware of many of these disparate pieces of the development process and use them to be successful in the project lifecycle.

你应该注意到 Janus 有两个头，不只是两张脸。这让 Janus 有额外的耳朵和眼睛来保持觉察。优秀的 IT 架构师会是卓越的倾听者和评估者。理解资本支出的原因对确定管理团队对组织未来的目标和愿景至关重要。用项目中要使用的设计和技术评估员工技术能力，有助于创建合适的培训和编程配对以确保项目成功。知道用哪些开源方案组合现成商用软件，可以大大简化项目时间线和预算。优秀架构师会觉察开发过程中这些不同部分，并用它们在项目生命周期中取得成功。

There are managers who demand and expect godlike qualities from their architects, but that is not the purpose of this comparison. A good architect is open to new ideas, tools and designs that progress the project, team, or profession; she doesn’t want to spend most of her time in management meetings or doing all the coding; she should concede to good ideas and cultivate an atmosphere for ideas to grow. It is an open mind that will succeed in architecture; a mind that can balance the many conflicting forces at work on projects. All architects strive to complete their projects and ensure the success of their development teams. The best architects create systems that stand the test of time because these systems are able to be maintained and expanded into the future as the organization grows and technology changes. These architects have listened, evaluated, and refactored their processes, designs, and methods to ensure the success of their work and projects; they have endeavored to ensure their products will withstand the transitions and changes that are sure to come.

有些经理要求并期望架构师有神一样的品质，但这不是这个比较的目的。好架构师对推进项目、团队或职业的新想法、工具和设计开放；她不想把大部分时间花在管理会议或写所有代码上；她应该向好想法让步、培育想法成长的氛围。开放的头脑才能在建筑中成功——能平衡项目上许多冲突力量的头脑。所有架构师都努力完成项目并确保开发团队成功。最好的架构师创建经得起时间考验的系统，因为这些系统能在组织成长和技术变化时被维护和扩展到未来。这些架构师倾听、评估并重构了他们的过程、设计和方法，以确保他们工作和项目的成功；他们努力确保他们的产品能承受必然到来的过渡和变化。

This is the mindset we should strive for as architects. It is simple yet difficult to perform. Like Janus, a software architect needs to be a keeper of doors and passageways, spanning the old and the new, incorporating creativity with sound engineering to fulfill today’s requirements while planning to meet tomorrow’s expectations.

这就是我们作为架构师应该追求的心态。它简单但难做。像 Janus 一样，软件架构师需要成为门和通道的守护者，跨越新旧，把创造力与健全工程结合，在满足今天需求的同时规划满足明天期望。

50. Architects' Focus Is on the Boundaries and Interfaces

作者：Einar Landre

Since Lord Nelson destroyed  the French and Spanish fleet at Trafalgar in 1805, “divide and conquer” has been the mantra for dealing with complex and difficult problems. A more familiar term with the same intent is separation of concern . From separation of concern we get encapsulation, and from encapsulation we get boundaries and interfaces.

自从 Nelson 勋爵 1805 年在特拉法加摧毁法西联合舰队，「分而治之」就一直是处理复杂困难问题的口头禅。同意思的更熟悉术语是关注点分离。从关注点分离我们得到封装，从封装我们得到边界和接口。

From an architect’s point of view, the hard part is to find the natural places to locate boundaries and define the appropriate interfaces needed to build a working system. This is especially difficult in large enterprise systems, often characterized by few natural boundaries and intertangled domains. In this situation, old wisdom such as “Minimize coupling, maximize cohesion” and “Do not slice through regions where high rates of information exchange are required” provide some guidance, but they say nothing about how to communicate the problems and potential solutions to stakeholders in a easy way.

从架构师角度看，难的是找到定位边界和定义构建可工作系统所需适当接口的自然位置。这在大型企业系统里尤其难，通常特征是很少自然边界、领域纠缠。这种情况下，「最小化耦合、最大化内聚」和「不要切过需要高信息交换率的区域」这些古老智慧提供一些指导，但它们对怎么用简单方式向干系人沟通问题和潜在解决方案一言不发。

Here the concept of bounded contexts and context mapping, as described by Eric Evans in his book Domain-Driven Design (Addison-Wesley Professional), comes to the rescue. A bounded context is an area where a model or concept is uniquely defined, and we represent it as a cloud or bubble with a descriptive name that defines its role and responsibility in the domain at hand. As an example, a shipping system might include contexts such as Cargo Operation, Cargo Scheduling, and Harbor Movement. In other domains, other names will be appropriate.

这里 Eric Evans 在《领域驱动设计》（Addison-Wesley Professional）里描述的限界上下文和上下文映射概念来救场。限界上下文是一个模型或概念被唯一定义的区域，我们把它表示为一个云或气泡，带一个描述性名称定义它在当前领域中的角色和责任。比如，一个航运系统可能包括货物操作、货物调度、港口移动等上下文。其他领域会有其他合适名称。

With the bounded contexts identified and drawn up on the whiteboard, it’s time to start to draw the relationships between the contexts. These relationships might address organizational, functional, or technical dependencies. The result from this exercise is a context map, a collection of bounded contexts and the interfaces between them.

识别出限界上下文并画在白板上后，就该开始画上下文之间的关系。这些关系可能处理组织、功能或技术依赖。这个练习的结果是上下文图——一组限界上下文及其之间的接口。

Such a context map provides architects with a powerful tool that allows them to focus on what belongs together and what should be kept apart, enabling them to divide and conquer wisely in a communicative way. The technique can easily be used to document and analyze the as-is situation, and from there guide redesign toward a better system characterized by low coupling, high cohesion, and well-defined interfaces.

这样的上下文图给架构师提供了强大工具，让他们聚焦什么该在一起、什么该分开，使他们能用沟通性的方式明智地分而治之。这个技术可以容易地用于记录和分析现状，并从那里引导重设计走向一个低耦合、高内聚、接口定义良好的更好系统。
